newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end lower after bank sale letdown.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end lower after bank sale letdown.

text.p: Caracas stocks on Friday extended a slide triggered by the government's suspension on Wednesday of Banco de Venezuela's long-expected sale, traders said.
"The bolsa's moving very cautiously and slowly," said Capital Market's broker Ricardo Marino.
The market's 19-share .IBC index lost 1.36 percent to close at 4,601.13 as 12.5 million shares worth one billion bolivars ($2 million) changed hands.
The successful sale of airline Aeropostal for $20 million to ALAS, a U.S.-Venezuelan consortium, on Friday did little to buoy market sentiment, traders said.
"Foreign investors are still digesting the shock of Banco de Venezuela's delayed sale, and many kept away anyway ahead of Monday's Labor Day holiday in the U.S.," said one trader.
Among issues that were traded, 18 fell, 11 rose and nine closed unchanged.
Volume was bolstered by a cross-trade of five million shares of Ceramica Carabobo. The stock closed down 0.10 bolivars at 15.65.
"Next week may see the bolsa rise again," Marino said. "The government's still making good noises about privatization."
